name: current practice, as documented in published Indonesian cases
order_point: days of cover at or below the lead time plus one review week
shelf_life_cap: one lot, aged stock not rotated first
notes: No forecast and no event calendar: the lot is sized from the rate the shelf is moving at today.
No safety-stock formula: the buffer is whatever the one-month lot happens to leave behind.
Every SKU is treated the same; there is no A/B/C service level.

sources.claim: Order when stock is nearly empty, quantity from experience, no ABC classification, every SKU treated alike; carrying cost benchmarked at the 8.05% BI rate; lead time 3 days at that firm
sources.case: PT ABC, 371 FMCG SKUs, March 2021 - February 2022
sources.ref: Savitri, Yulianti & Pambudi (2022), Jurnal Rekayasa Sistem dan Industri 9(2), doi:10.25124/jrsi.v9i02.584

sources.claim: Weekly ordering cadence, orders placed at the start of each week, distribution requirements planning
sources.case: FMCG distribution case, Jurnal Ilmiah Teknik Industri
sources.ref: Luju (2020), Jurnal Ilmiah Teknik Industri, Universitas Merdeka Malang

sources.claim: Inventory held 43.73 days in 2016 rising to 56.67 days in 2025 (DIO) at an Indonesian FMCG manufacturer
sources.case: PT Indofood CBP Sukses Makmur Tbk, 2016-2025
sources.ref: Feranika et al. (2026), Jurnal Manajemen Terapan dan Keuangan 15(3)

sources.claim: Out-of-stock averages about 8% across four decades of retail audits; 8.3% in physical stores in the GMA study
Supermarket shrink 2.70% of retail sales, range 1.76%-3.10% (all causes, not expiry alone)
